### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s).

**55** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 357fb1ea45b684e339a2f375523c99ae21f6b4c4`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (44 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (symbol, 55 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 55 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 357fb1ea45b684e339a2f375523c99ae21f6b4c4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aec6e90b9546da38f8aacd2712b59c2b10382eb8` — the merge of head `504662ea13e6d593c2ffca26ca97091c59da0972` into base `357fb1ea45b684e339a2f375523c99ae21f6b4c4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aec6e90b9546da38f8aacd2712b59c2b10382eb8 && git checkout aec6e90b9546da38f8aacd2712b59c2b10382eb8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 357fb1ea45b684e339a2f375523c99ae21f6b4c4 504662ea13e6d593c2ffca26ca97091c59da0972 && git checkout -B drift-repro 357fb1ea45b684e339a2f375523c99ae21f6b4c4 && git merge --no-ff 504662ea13e6d593c2ffca26ca97091c59da0972

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 357fb1ea45b684e339a2f375523c99ae21f6b4c4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 357fb1ea45b684e339a2f375523c99ae21f6b4c4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-18T00:47Z

Head-sha: 504662ea13e6d593c2ffca26ca97091c59da0972
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for #34766 PR-a (claim 6963760223 with the seat's rulings D1 to D4, os-dev report 6965441769).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Part of #34766`, base `main`. Seven paths, +844/-0:
- the new `domains/mcp-authoring.ts` and its test;
- a 9-line injection in `domains/mcp.ts`;
- the collision pin in `skill-md-surface-guard.test.ts`;
- the add-only design note;
- one `DISPATCHER_DOMAINS` row;
- a `@objectstack/runtime` patch changeset.

The `check-route-envelope.mjs` row is outside the claimed surface. The gate demands it, and o3-E approved it. Not governed. The module is not re-exported from `@objectstack/runtime`'s index.

**CI.** It was still running when I read it (22 pending, nothing failed). The runtime typecheck was not measured locally, so this verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

**D1 A, the intersection: held.** `resolveOpenAuthoringInjection` decides as follows.
- **The token half.** A grant without `metadata:write` gets `undefined`, and no grant read is made. An API key or a session carries no grant array, so it gets `undefined` too.
- **No user, fail closed.** An envelope with no `userId` gets `undefined`.
- **The human half.** `humanHoldsAuthoringCapability` resolves the user's own grants through `resolveUserAuthzGrants(ql, userId, { tenantId })`. The tenant is the organization the token's consent bound. The grants are judged by `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict({ systemPermissions, operation: 'save' })`. It never reads the envelope's `isSystem` or its `systemPermissions`, so an agent envelope cannot lend itself the capability.
- **A throw, fail closed.** No data engine, or a resolution that throws, gives `false` with one `warn`.
- **The four cells are pinned:**
  - a token without scope (no registry, and the grant is never read);
  - a user without the grant (no tool listed, and a call is refused 403 before any read);
  - both halves (the three tools listed, and a read served);
  - an API key (no registry).

  On top of those, no user, a throwing resolution, and a call stamped with another user than the one admitted are each pinned to refuse.

**One verdict for the listing and the call: held.** The registry closes over `admitted` and `userId`. `getAll()` lists the three tools only when admitted. `execute` checks `admitted` and that `context.principal.userId` equals the admitted user, before it reads any argument or the protocol. A refused user is listed nothing, and a call that slips through gets `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`.

**D3 A, the names: held.** The tools are `list_metadata_items`, `get_metadata_item` and `list_drafts`. The new guard pin registers them beside the full native surface under every scope with no collision, and one runtime pin checks them against the hosted platform tool names. `list_drafts` serves no verdicts, which belong to PR-b.

**The reads.**
- **Environment routing.** The protocol comes from `deps.resolveService(context, 'protocol', context.environmentId)`, so the per-environment kernel is selected the way `/meta` selects it. The protocol reads its environment off the instance, never off the request (`protocol-door-requests.ts:75`).
- **`list_metadata_items`** refuses an undeclared type through the same `refuseUnknownMetaListType` the `/meta` list uses (`INVALID_REQUEST`). It reads with `previewDrafts` unless `state: 'active'`, and filters to drafts on `state: 'draft'`.
- **`get_metadata_item`** reads the draft in place of the published item by default, the draft only on `state: 'draft'`, and answers 404 for nothing found.
- **`list_drafts`** passes `package` as `packageId`, with no organization (ADR-0131 D6).
- **Refusals.** A coded refusal under 500 keeps its code. Anything else is `INTERNAL_ERROR`, with the text logged and never served.

**The injection and the note.** `handleMcpRequest` resolves the injection per request and spreads `authoring` only when it is defined. The design note is add-only, dated, and names the D3 ruling and the colliding tool's file.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. Clause-② is `yes (widening)`.** The claim reasons "no published accept set or spec export changes", and that is true of exports, since the module is not on the package index. But the open runtime's MCP door now serves three tools it did not serve to a `metadata:write` client whose user holds `manage_metadata`, and accepts calls to them. That is the same reading I applied on #35043, where filled answer members and new instruction texts were a widening. Please amend the claim, the PR body and the changeset to `Clause-②: yes (widening: three MCP tools served to a metadata:write client whose user holds manage_metadata)`, and keep `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch`. If the seat rules on #35043 that served-surface changes are not Clause-②, that ruling closes this item too.

### Notes
- N1. **For the seat's L2.** The reads are "unmasked" on the claim that the admission predicate (`metaWriteCapabilityVerdict`, operation `save`) admits no one whom `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt` and `mayReadPendingDrafts` would refuse. That is asserted in the docblock, but no pin ties the three predicates together. This door also bypasses `createMetaListAnswer` (the per-caller list gate, the locale collapse, the mask, translation), so `meta-list-projection-parity.test.ts` does not see it. For an authoring read of source definitions, the untranslated summary is right. The L2 should confirm that the admission predicate implies the other two, or ask for a pin that it does.
- N2. Every request from a `metadata:write` token whose envelope has a user now makes one grant resolution before the MCP server is built, even a request that calls only data tools. That is the price of "judged afresh" on a stateless door, and it is acceptable. If it shows in latency, that read is the one to memoise per token for the request's lifetime.

Next: S1 (text only), then the seat's fable L2 (D1 touches the authoring gate), then the landing tier read on the final file list. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `504662ea13e6d593c2ffca26ca97091c59da0972`
Local-runs: none

PR #35059 (PR-a of card #34766), declaration face plus the admission rule. Read: the card body and its five comments, the PR body, the 7-file net diff against `main` (+844/-0), and the head's check-runs. Code outside the diff was read at the head tree to judge the diff's claims, never reviewed. Two findings are must-fix (M1, M2), so the verdict is FAIL; the admission rule itself (D1) is right.

Check-runs on the head at review time: 30 completed `success`, the rest `skipped`, and 8 still `in_progress` (Test Core 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 of 10; Type Check · workspace; Type Check · consumer gates). No run concluded red. The runtime typecheck the dev declared NOT MEASURED locally is therefore still unanswered by CI; this record does not rest on it.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Served tool surface: three new tools under `metadata:write`. RIGHT as built, declared WRONG (see ②).** `list_metadata_items`, `get_metadata_item`, `list_drafts` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts:83`), each with a closed input schema (`additionalProperties: false`). Before this diff `domains/mcp.ts` passed no `authoring`, so every one of these names answered as an unknown tool. That is a widening of what the published `@objectstack/runtime` exposes and accepts.

2. **D1, the four cells. RIGHT.** All four are pinned through the real `handleMcpRequest`, with envelopes from the real `resolveExecutionContext` (`mcp-authoring.test.ts`):
   - token without `metadata:write`: no `authoring` member handed, no grant read (`mcp-authoring.ts:227`);
   - `metadata:write`, user without `manage_metadata`: `getAll()` is empty, a direct call is refused 403 before any protocol call (`:296`, `:310`);
   - both: three tools listed, a read served, and the test asserts the envelope's own `systemPermissions` is empty, so the verdict came from the human's grants (`:272`, `isSystem` not passed);
   - API key: no `authoring` member, no grant read, even with `manage_metadata` on the envelope.
   The token half stays with `grantsAuthoringTools` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:2499`, re-asked in `registerAuthoringTools`, `mcp-server-runtime.ts:1727`); the runtime's copy at `:227` can only withhold, never admit. An omitted organization admits nothing stored (`ResolveUserAuthzGrantsOptions.tenantId`: "no every-organization reading"), so a token with no bound organization fails closed too.

3. **Fail closed. RIGHT.** No `userId` returns `undefined` before any lookup (`:231`, pinned, ablation 3). A throwing resolution or a missing engine is caught and returns `false` with one `warn` (`:265-281`, pinned, ablation 2); `resolveUserAuthzGrants` raises `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` on a failed store read instead of an empty grant set, and that lands in the same catch. A call stamped with another user is refused (`:310`, pinned).

4. **The 403 shape. RIGHT.** `isError: true` with text `{ "error": { code, message, status } }`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403, no `details`: the envelope `codedErrorResult` gives every coded MCP refusal (`mcp-http-tools.ts`), and the listing rule matches the federation pair's (#28938): one verdict read by the listing and by each call. In practice the SDK answers an unlisted tool as unknown, so the 403 is the defensive second read; that is what the body claims.

5. **D3 names. RIGHT.** `list_metadata_items` / `get_metadata_item`; `list_drafts` keeps the design name. Pinned against `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` and the family prefixes, and against the full native surface under every scope (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md-surface-guard.test.ts`). The design note is add-only, dated, one paragraph.

6. **N1, the "unmasked" claim. Partly RIGHT, partly WRONG.**
   - The narrow implication holds by construction. `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict` admits on `manage_metadata` (`packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts:91-104`); `OBJECT_SCHEMA_WRITE_CAPABILITIES` is `['manage_metadata']` and is spread into `OBJECT_SCHEMA_MASK_EXEMPT_CAPABILITIES` (`object-schema-fls.ts:93`, `:143-146`); `mayReadPendingDrafts` is a bare delegation to `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt` (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:1816-1818`). The composition is already pinned (`object-schema-fls.test.ts:183-186`). No caller can hold the save grant without the mask exemption and the drafts admission, so no new pin is owed for that. One nit: the two sides spell the capability through two constants (`METADATA_AUTHORING_CAPABILITY` and `OBJECT_SCHEMA_WRITE_CAPABILITIES`) that agree only by literal.
   - **M1 (must-fix, or a seat ruling).** The header's sentence "That is the `/meta` doors' own answer for this caller" (`mcp-authoring.ts:49`) is false for five types. The object mask is not the only per-caller read rule on `/meta`. `createMetaItemReadGate` and `createMetaListReadGate` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:1688-1865`, `:1944-2040`) judge on the caller's `systemPermissions` and audience, with no `manage_metadata` exemption:
     - `dashboard`: `requiredPermissions` the caller lacks is refused whole, 403 (`:1772`), "on every door and to an author as to anyone";
     - `view`: a list view whose `requiredPermissions` the caller lacks is refused whole (`:1796`); the author exemption covers a container's entries only, on the stored-version doors;
     - `app`: an app-level `requiredPermissions` or an unpublished app is refused "either way, author or not" (`MetaReadGatePolicy.app`, ruling 5856774816);
     - `book` / `doc`: the ADR-0046 audience (`:1833`, `:1843`), 403 for a non-audience caller, no author arm at all.
     This door calls `getMetaItem` / `getMetaItems` directly (`mcp-authoring.ts:335`, `:349`) and runs neither gate. So `get_metadata_item` hands a `manage_metadata` holder the full body of a doc outside their audience, or a dashboard, list view or app they lack the capability for, which every `/meta` door refuses that same human; `list_metadata_items` lists them. D1 ruled who is served the tools, not what the reads withhold, and no ruling on the card widens these reads. Fix: judge each read through the gates `@objectstack/rest` already exports (`createMetaItemReadGate`, `createMetaListReadGate`, `packages/rest/src/index.ts:165-168`) with a caller built from the resolved human's grants, and pin one refused cell; or take a seat ruling that this door is whole-for-author on those types and correct the header. Either way a pin is owed: today nothing ties the door to the `/meta` read gates.

7. **Nothing of PR-b leaked. RIGHT.** No save or discard tool, no verdict on `list_drafts` (its description promises none), no `walledCatalogWriteVerdict`, no public verdict method, no `initialize` or skill-md text, no `packages/metadata-protocol` or `packages/spec` change. The module is not on the package entry (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts` exports nothing from it), so the package's export surface is unchanged.

8. Nits (no effect on the contract):
   - `refusalFromThrown` (`:396`) folds a coded 5xx (a store outage's 503) into `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`;
   - it is a second reader of coded throws beside `thrownRefusalEnvelope`, without the `isSandboxCrash` arm; no sandboxed body is reachable from these three reads today;
   - the tool descriptions say "in this environment" and name no organization; correct per ADR-0131 D6.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/34766-mcp-open-draft-door-read.md`: `@objectstack/runtime` `patch`. The level is RIGHT: a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3). `@objectstack/mcp` moves a test file only and publishes nothing; the design doc and the gate table publish nothing. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: RIGHT. Nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- **M2 (must-fix, text only).** `Clause-②: no`, in the PR body and the changeset body, is WRONG. CONTRIBUTING.md item 5 asks whether the change widens "what a published package accepts or exposes (its accept set or public surface)". Three newly served tools with new input schemas widen both; the changeset's own first sentence says an OAuth client "now gets three read tools". The claim's reason ("no published accept set or spec export changes") reads the question as exports only. Both bodies owe the line `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The level stays `patch`. No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition are owed (widening, not narrowing). `Check Changeset` passing does not answer this: it reads the line's form, not its truth.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions` (one entry, report 6965345893): `check:route-envelope` demands a `DISPATCHER_DOMAINS` line outside the claimed surface.** Answered: option A, applied as `'mcp-authoring.ts': { handBuilt: 0 }` (`scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs:1107`). Correct: the module builds MCP tool results and no REST body, the same declaration the sibling helper modules carry, and the PR body names it under "Outside the claimed surface" in the gate's words. `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` concluded `success`. The final report's `open_questions` is empty.
- **Dev flag: `@objectstack/runtime` typecheck NOT MEASURED locally.** Not yet answered: `Type Check · workspace` and `Type Check · consumer gates` are `in_progress` on this head. Owed before landing, by the check-run, not by a local run.
- **Dev flag: comment 6965425382 is a byte-for-byte duplicate of the blocked report.** Answered: superseded by 6965441769; no effect on the diff.
- **Dev flag: `initialize` instructions and skill-md unchanged.** Answered: right for PR-a; the design assigns those texts to the save and the verdict, which are PR-b.
- **Dev flag: `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` not applied.** Answered: right; it gates writes and no `/meta` read asks it.
- **N2, one grant read per `metadata:write` request.** Answered with its reason: the HTTP door is stateless and each request is judged afresh (header, `:14-16`); a token without the scope, an API key and a session cost no read (pinned). Acceptable. It is not an id materialisation or a join.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).** No new id materialisation and no in-app join. One should-fix: `list_metadata_items` with `state: "draft"` reads the type's whole draft-overlaid list and keeps the drafts in memory (`mcp-authoring.ts:335-341`), where `listDrafts({ type })` (already on `OpenAuthoringProtocol`, `:171-173`) asks the store for exactly those rows and returns the same summary fields. No reason is given for the in-app filter.
- **Escalated to the seat: M1.** The choice between running the `/meta` read gates and ruling the door whole-for-author is a contract decision D1–D4 did not take.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34766-mcp-draft-door-read`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
